newsitem.title: UK: BA eyes Europe's low fare airline market.
newsitem.headline: BA eyes Europe's low fare airline market.

text.p: British Airways Plc confirmed on Friday that it has commissioned a new study into what impact new low-fare airlines might be having on the European airline market for leisure travel.

But BA declined to comment on a report in today's Finacial Times newspaper that it was thinking of either setting up its own 'no-frills' carrier or taking over an existing operator, such as Britain's EasyJet, to compete.

"All we have done is ask an advertising and marketing agency, Howell Henry Caldecott & Lewry, to carry out some market research into the European leisure air travel market and the advent of low-cost carriers," said a company spokesman.
"We have done various studies and this is just another one...Once it is complete we will analyse it and see what it means for BA," he said.

Completion of Europe's free market for air travel in April is expected to see the creation of more low-cost niche market airlines, offering cut-price, no-frills services afforded by lower staff costs, minimal catering and use of cheaper regional airports.

BA has long been developing a network of franchised services operated by low-cost, local airlines on regional routes, and also has four leisure routes from London Gatwick to the Bahamas, Puerto Rica and Florida operated by a holiday airline, Flying Colours.
